analysis:
This batch changes documentation only. No provider source is included.

What the docs now describe:
- docs/provider/quickstart.md head 65-71 and 113-116: once the operator consents, Autopilot may download catalog models on the operator's behalf. Builds downloaded later join the Autopilot set at the next start with no new consent step. Before this PR, the docs said enrollment never downloads models.
- docs/reference/configuration.md head 180-186 (patch hunk @@ -177,7 +177,13):
  - [backend.autopilot_downloads] enabled defaults to on when absent, but applies only with saved Autopilot consent.
  - max_storage_gb and max_models are uncapped by default.
  - reserve_gb defaults to 50 GiB of free disk.
  - Changing download settings does not change the Autopilot revision.
  - The provider writes an owner-only ledger, autopilot-downloads.json, holding up to 256 entries.
  - Downloaded builds stay in the set when the catalog is unreachable, and nothing deletes their files.
  - Scheduled windows keep previously verified builds while their bytes still hash unchanged.

Security relevance:
- This is new automated surface touching model integrity and availability: A-004 model weights, T-012 and T-027 weight substitution, T-016 disk exhaustion.
- It also touches the consent scope. Quickstart line 106 says consent covers the shadow rollout, not active residency control, yet the download behavior extends beyond that.
- The docs claim downloads are verified catalog builds with weight-hash checks. That keeps the existing weight-hash verification as the integrity control.
- The ledger lets Autopilot keep serving builds while the catalog is unreachable. Integration should verify that a retired or revoked catalog build cannot remain served solely through ledger state. The configuration doc says retired builds are excluded at enrollment.

Why no finding:
- The implementing sources are not in this batch: AutopilotDownloadSettings.swift, AutopilotDownload.swift, AutopilotDownloadLedger.swift, ProviderLoop+AutopilotModelSet.swift and ScheduledWindowSelection.swift.
- So I cannot confirm any regression in hash verification, catalog revocation handling, the owner-only ledger permissions, or disk guards.
- No change touches T-041 or the cache, the attestation boundaries (TB-009, TB-011) or auth tokens (A-008).

Open questions for integration:
- Does the canonical threat model need an entry for Autopilot-initiated downloads? Relevant points are default-on with no cap, and joining the serving set without fresh consent.
- Does the code enforce the documented verification, revocation and consent gating?
